analysis: Examined scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh (head lines 11-60, 86-91) and the test edits. The resolver now accepts a branch push only as master+staging or dev+dev, and it fails closed on any other ref or environment. A push still never selects prod (lines 67-70), and validation_only is forced false for pushes. The new check at lines 55-58 means a dev release can only come from a dev-branch push, since master or dispatch dev is allowed only as a validation build with publish=false. I found no bypass: the RELEASE_RESUME_RUN_ID early exec at line 5 is unchanged, and RELEASE_VERSION_OVERRIDE is cleared for pushes. Dev-push versions get -dev.branch.N, which check-release-version.sh already accepts via (branch\.)?. The test files only restate the new routing: master push gives staging, the dev lane is dispatch+validation only, and the dev release comes from release-dev-branch.yml. They also add assertions that the final app meets the self-updater designated requirement (team SLDQ2GJ6TL, bundle io.darkbloom.provider) and that the source gate receives RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT. Unverified: the caller workflow, release-provider.yml, release-dev-branch.yml, provider-release-resume.py verify-source and the repository's dev-branch protection were not supplied. The test comment at about line 381 says nothing signs ad-hoc, including the dev-branch lane. That implies dev-branch pushes are now signed with the production Developer ID identity, which the self-updater trusts for any environment. Whether verify-source and branch protection gate dev-branch content as strictly as master is outside this evidence, so I recorded it as an open question (T-013/T-034/T-054 area) rather than a finding. Further review should confirm the dev lane's signing, notarization and publish credentials are scoped so that dev-branch code cannot reach production release registration or the production update channel.
